wada.text: Prohibited at all times. Named in S0 (non-approved substances).

mechanism: Proposed effects on blood-vessel growth and nitric oxide pathways, from animal and lab studies.
humanEvidence: 2025 systematic review (orthopaedic sports medicine): 36 studies, 35 preclinical and 1 clinical; no clinical safety data; half-life under 30 minutes

The one human report is a retrospective, uncontrolled knee-pain chart review (16 patients): 11 of 12 given BPC-157 alone and 75% of 4 given BPC-157 plus thymosin beta-4 reported significant improvement; no control group
2026 orthopaedic primer: tendon and muscle findings are largely unvalidated in human trials
Rat combination study (2026, 32 rats, Achilles repair): BPC-157 alone gave numerically better scores without reaching significance; adding TB-500 gave no extra benefit over either alone

FDA briefing (July 2026) listed three adverse-event reports after BPC-157 injection (for example injection-site redness and swelling, and shortness of breath needing an ER visit); FDA said cause could not be established

A health-record study found 1,039 documented BPC-157 users, with new users up 33-fold from 2020 to 2026; the first randomized, placebo-controlled pilot (after rotator-cuff repair, NCT07803250) is scheduled to start January 2027
proven: Nothing proven in controlled human trials
unproven: Tendon, ligament, muscle, gut or joint healing in humans (animal data only, plus uncontrolled reports)
unknown: Human safety profile, including long-term effects
Any effective or safe human dose
Product purity and content of unregulated products

doseInfo.regimen: No established human dose (no published controlled human trials; Health Canada also states there are no established human dosing protocols)

safetyConcerns: No clinical safety data in humans (systematic review)

Unregulated production: contamination and mislabelling risks (Health Canada advisories list infection, contaminants, liver or kidney damage, blood clots and tumour growth among risks of unauthorized peptides)
evidenceLevel: Animal data; very limited uncontrolled human reports; no controlled trials

statusDetail.healthCanada: Not authorized. KPV is named in Health Canada's 2026 advisory on unauthorized injectable peptides, and 'Klow 80 MG' products containing KPV were seized in December 2025.
statusDetail.fda: Not FDA-approved. FDA states it has not identified any human exposure data on drug products containing KPV, by any route, and lacks important safety information. Not FDA-approved. FDA removed it from the Category 2 'significant safety risk' compounding list in April 2026; an FDA advisory committee (PCAC) narrowly recommended it for the 503A bulks list in July 2026 against FDA staff advice; HHS published an interim enforcement-discretion policy for the six recommended peptides (Federal Register, 2026-10-30). Enforcement discretion is not approval.

wada.text: Not named on the 2026 List. S0 (non-approved substances) covers any pharmacological substance not addressed elsewhere on the List and with no current approval by any government health regulator for human therapeutic use; it is prohibited at all times. The 2027 List (in force 2027-01-01) names 'peptides' in general in S0.

mechanism: Tripeptide Lys-Pro-Val, the C-terminal end (residues 11-13) of alpha-MSH. In cell studies it enters gut and immune cells through the PepT1 transporter and dampens NF-kB and MAP-kinase inflammatory signalling.
humanEvidence: No human studies: FDA identified no human exposure data, and its review found no human clinical studies for the proposed uses (wound healing, inflammatory conditions)

Cell studies (2008): nanomolar KPV reduced NF-kB and MAP-kinase activation and inflammatory cytokine release in intestinal epithelial and immune cells, via PepT1, a transporter induced in the colon during inflammatory bowel disease

Mouse studies (2008): oral KPV reduced chemically induced (DSS and TNBS) colitis; in DSS and transfer colitis it sped recovery, and in DSS colitis it rescued all treated MC1R-deficient mice, suggesting effects partly independent of MC1R
unproven: Gut, skin or anti-inflammatory benefits in people
unknown: Human safety and any human dose
What adding KPV to other peptides (as in KLOW) does
safetyConcerns: FDA lacks important information on safety issues, including whether it would cause harm
evidenceLevel: Cell and mouse studies only; no human data
